18.01.01.context: An authenticated profile uploader submits a PNG avatar for a private account.
18.01.01.failure: Checking only client-side file extension and Content-Type allows renamed or oversized uploads.
18.01.01.correction: Enforce size, extension, declared MIME and byte signature on the server before quarantine.
18.01.01.positive: A well-formed PNG enters a quarantined state with an explicit size and type.
18.01.01.negative: A forged PDF-as-PNG, executable extension or oversized object fails before persistence.
18.01.01.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.02.context: A team uploads invoices where a valid filename can disguise arbitrary executable bytes.
18.01.02.failure: Trusting the browser MIME header causes a renamed PDF or executable to pass image validation.
18.01.02.correction: Inspect actual leading bytes against a fixed allowed-signature table and reject mismatches.
18.01.02.positive: A PDF with matching signature and declared type passes the initial teaching gate.
18.01.02.negative: A PNG filename containing PDF bytes is rejected even when the request advertises image/png.
18.01.02.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.03.context: A browser requests one short-lived upload capability for its own tenant workspace.
18.01.03.failure: An unscoped token remains valid for any user and may be replayed after its expiration.
18.01.03.correction: Sign a tenant/user/filename/nonce/expiry claim and verify binding before accepting an upload intent.
18.01.03.positive: The intended actor can validate a token during its short validity window.
18.01.03.negative: Another tenant, another user, an altered token or an expired token is denied.
18.01.03.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.04.context: An employee requests a previously scanned private HR document from object storage.
18.01.04.failure: Listing an object key directly or treating an upload receipt as read authorization bypasses tenant checks.
18.01.04.correction: Reauthorize every read using authenticated tenant, owner and clean-scan state.
18.01.04.positive: The owner can read an asset only after it is explicitly marked clean.
18.01.04.negative: A foreign tenant or owner and every quarantined or blocked asset are inaccessible.
18.01.04.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.05.context: A product site accepts camera originals and needs responsive thumbnails.
18.01.05.failure: Decoding an untrusted megapixel image without pixel limits risks decompression bombs and resource exhaustion.
18.01.05.correction: Plan a sandboxed image worker with pixel ceilings, EXIF stripping and deterministic output dimensions.
18.01.05.positive: An instructor can specify a worker contract with width, height, byte and metadata limits.
18.01.05.negative: An image exceeding pixel ceilings or a decoder error must be quarantined without any public derivative.
18.01.05.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.06.context: A document pipeline quarantines PDFs until an asynchronous scanner gives a verdict.
18.01.06.failure: Treating a scanner timeout as clean leaks malicious files through a fail-open status.
18.01.06.correction: Keep assets quarantined until an explicit clean verdict and block malicious or failed scans.
18.01.06.positive: A clean scan transitions a quarantined asset to a readable state.
18.01.06.negative: A failed scan or malicious verdict stays blocked and never gains read permissions.
18.01.06.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.07.context: A media upload triggers metadata extraction, thumbnails and retention jobs.
18.01.07.failure: Running costly processing synchronously on request threads causes duplicate work after retries.
18.01.07.correction: Enqueue a deduplicated processing job and move assets through monotonic quarantine states.
18.01.07.positive: A repeated upload intent is scoped and a clean processed asset becomes readable.
18.01.07.negative: A retry cannot make a failed scan clean or leak an asset while processing is incomplete.
18.01.07.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.01.08.context: A capstone marketplace stores user pictures and private PDF receipts in the same account.
18.01.08.failure: A single public bucket and filename-only validation expose receipts and unsafe content.
18.01.08.correction: Compose server validation, scoped intents, quarantined scanning and per-request read authorization.
18.01.08.positive: The complete teaching pipeline accepts safe assets and checks owner access after scanning.
18.01.08.negative: A cross-tenant request, MIME spoof or scanner failure never exposes a receipt.
18.01.08.caveat: These are byte-signature and state-machine teaching controls only: real image decoders, antivirus engines, durable object storage and provider URL signing require separate qualification.

18.02.01.context: A billing app sends receipts and optional promotional campaigns to the same account.
18.02.01.failure: Applying marketing consent rules to receipts or bypassing consent for offers confuses legal purposes.
18.02.01.correction: Separate transactional and marketing message intents; require positive opt-in before marketing enqueue and claim.
18.02.01.positive: An opted-in user gets a marketing job and every authorized purchase can create a receipt.
18.02.01.negative: An opted-out user never gets a claimed marketing send even if consent is revoked after enqueue.
18.02.01.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.02.context: A team uses React Email to render branded password reset and receipt templates.
18.02.02.failure: Interpolating raw user-provided HTML into email templates creates unsafe markup and broken links.
18.02.02.correction: Use escaped React component props, allowlisted links and preview/snapshot review for every template.
18.02.02.positive: An instructor reviews a static HTML template with escaped display names and stable links.
18.02.02.negative: HTML injection, untrusted redirect URLs and accidental tracking in security mail fail the review.
18.02.02.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.03.context: A SaaS platform switches between two email delivery providers without changing domain code.
18.02.03.failure: Directly importing one vendor SDK into every route prevents timeout policy and provider substitution.
18.02.03.correction: Define a send adapter with deterministic idempotency keys, typed outcomes and redacted provider errors.
18.02.03.positive: A fake adapter accepts a canonical job and returns a normalized acknowledged status.
18.02.03.negative: A vendor outage cannot silently mutate a previously acknowledged job to failed.
18.02.03.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.04.context: An email provider posts bounce and complaint events for previously accepted messages.
18.02.04.failure: Applying unverified provider webhooks lets strangers suppress users or forge delivery metrics.
18.02.04.correction: Verify exact raw-body signatures, timestamp freshness and provider-scoped delivery IDs before recording status.
18.02.04.positive: A signed delivery event enters the inbox once and can be processed independently.
18.02.04.negative: A modified body or duplicated delivery event is rejected or deduplicated.
18.02.04.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.05.context: A production email domain must prove authorized sender identity and protect reputation.
18.02.05.failure: Assuming an SMTP API key alone authenticates a From domain omits DNS and alignment controls.
18.02.05.correction: Document SPF authorization, DKIM signatures and DMARC alignment with DNS verification evidence.
18.02.05.positive: A real staging domain can demonstrate aligned SPF or DKIM and a monitored DMARC policy.
18.02.05.negative: Missing alignment, a broad SPF record or a forged From domain fails release review.
18.02.05.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.06.context: A checkout handler retries when a provider send response is lost after commit.
18.02.06.failure: Generating a fresh message ID on each retry duplicates receipts and password-reset notifications.
18.02.06.correction: Persist a tenant/user-scoped logical send key and reconcile unknown outcomes before retry.
18.02.06.positive: Repeated scheduling with the same key resolves to one outbox job.
18.02.06.negative: Reusing the key for a different template is rejected rather than mutating the original message.
18.02.06.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.07.context: A mailing worker receives a 429 response while many campaigns compete for capacity.
18.02.07.failure: Immediate retries without a budget amplify outages and exhaust provider quotas.
18.02.07.correction: Apply bounded exponential backoff, attempt ceilings and an inspectable dead-letter status.
18.02.07.positive: A temporary failure waits before the next send attempt and eventually succeeds.
18.02.07.negative: A permanently failing message stops after the retry budget; it cannot loop forever.
18.02.07.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.02.08.context: A course registration sends a confirmation email and receives a provider delivery callback.
18.02.08.failure: Directly calling a production mail API from a demo hides consent, duplicate and retry risks.
18.02.08.correction: Demonstrate consent-aware local outbox enqueue, claim/settle and authenticated webhook inbox transitions.
18.02.08.positive: The local fixture records one transactional confirmation and one verified delivery event.
18.02.08.negative: Duplicate jobs, forged bounce webhooks and marketing messages without opt-in are denied.
18.02.08.caveat: The teaching outbox does not send an email, inspect DNS, run React Email, or connect to a delivery provider; these are independent live release gates.

18.03.01.context: A multi-tenant knowledge base needs searchable project titles and descriptions in PostgreSQL.
18.03.01.failure: Using raw ILIKE expressions everywhere misses linguistic ranking and consistent query plans.
18.03.01.correction: Design a PostgreSQL tsvector column, language config, GIN index and tenant-scoped tsquery filters.
18.03.01.positive: A real PostgreSQL qualification will compare indexed FTS results and plans against expected tenant fixtures.
18.03.01.negative: A query for tenant A must not return tenant B documents even when text matches.
18.03.01.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.02.context: A support search should match misspelled account names and partial terms.
18.03.02.failure: Substring-only matching forces full scans and cannot score fuzzy candidate similarity.
18.03.02.correction: Compare pg_trgm similarity, GIN/GiST indexes and sensible minimum thresholds on realistic data.
18.03.02.positive: A dedicated PostgreSQL test can show a typo match and measure its query plan.
18.03.02.negative: A loose similarity threshold must not expose hidden or another tenant's records.
18.03.02.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.03.context: A documentation portal ranks title matches above incidental paragraph matches.
18.03.03.failure: Returning rows in insertion order makes relevance unpredictable across data changes.
18.03.03.correction: Define deterministic title/body weights, stable tie breaks and a documented relevance test set.
18.03.03.positive: The local tenant-search fixture ranks a title match above a body-only match.
18.03.03.negative: A lower-value body match must not unpredictably outrank an exact title hit.
18.03.03.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.04.context: An account needs paginated and status-filtered search across thousands of notes.
18.03.04.failure: A client-supplied offset without a tenant filter or stable index snapshot can leak or skip rows.
18.03.04.correction: Bind tenant, filters, query and revision into pagination state and invalidate it after mutation.
18.03.04.positive: Two pages return deterministic results for the same scoped query and index revision.
18.03.04.negative: A cursor from another tenant or a stale index revision is rejected.
18.03.04.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.05.context: Search documents are updated by asynchronous webhooks and can arrive out of order.
18.03.05.failure: An older indexing event overwrites a newer title or resurrects a deleted document.
18.03.05.correction: Require monotonic document revisions and tombstones so stale events are no-ops.
18.03.05.positive: A version-two update survives later arrival of version-one data.
18.03.05.negative: A deleted record cannot be resurrected by replaying a stale indexing event.
18.03.05.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.06.context: A startup must choose between PostgreSQL FTS, Meilisearch and Typesense.
18.03.06.failure: Choosing an external search cluster for every small app adds operational cost and consistency failure modes.
18.03.06.correction: Compare query needs, typo support, tenant boundaries, operational burden and indexing latency before switching engines.
18.03.06.positive: A decision record identifies when PostgreSQL FTS is enough and when a dedicated engine is justified.
18.03.06.negative: No external engine is claimed production-ready without real tenancy and consistency tests.
18.03.06.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.07.context: A search dashboard logs popular queries and zero-result rate across organizations.
18.03.07.failure: Logging full query strings and result bodies may expose passwords, health information and private records.
18.03.07.correction: Aggregate per-tenant metrics with retention limits and scrubbed sensitive values.
18.03.07.positive: An analytics design records counts and latency without raw personal query text.
18.03.07.negative: A cross-tenant dashboard or raw-secret query log fails the privacy review.
18.03.07.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.03.08.context: A help-center search box must remain correct through index updates and paging.
18.03.08.failure: A visually fast search can still show stale results or foreign tenant content.
18.03.08.correction: Combine scoped indexing, deterministic ranking, bounded pages and invalidation on revision change.
18.03.08.positive: The local lab returns ranked results and a valid second page for a stable index.
18.03.08.negative: A stale cursor, hidden record or foreign tenant result is not returned.
18.03.08.caveat: The in-memory scorer is not PostgreSQL FTS, pg_trgm, Meilisearch or Typesense. Benchmark indexing, relevance and real SQL RLS independently.

18.04.01.context: A payments integration needs an API token for a third-party provider.
18.04.01.failure: Sending the provider secret to a browser or logging headers gives every client global privileges.
18.04.01.correction: Keep credentials server-only, bind outgoing requests to allowlisted hosts and redact operational logs.
18.04.01.positive: A production adapter plan separates public request input from server-owned provider authentication.
18.04.01.negative: A browser bundle containing private credentials or an arbitrary outbound URL blocks release.
18.04.01.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.02.context: A billing provider sends signed event payloads with retryable delivery.
18.04.02.failure: Parsing and reserializing webhook JSON before signature verification invalidates or weakens authenticity checks.
18.04.02.correction: HMAC the exact received bytes plus provider timestamp and use constant-time digest comparison.
18.04.02.positive: A correctly signed raw payload is accepted once within the freshness window.
18.04.02.negative: Modified bytes, a stale timestamp or invalid signature cannot create a trusted event.
18.04.02.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.03.context: An unreliable tax API slows checkout and returns intermittent 5xx responses.
18.04.03.failure: Unlimited retries on synchronous requests worsen outages and can charge customers repeatedly.
18.04.03.correction: Use timeout budgets, safe retry classifications, capped attempts and a circuit-breaker state model.
18.04.03.positive: The training outbox shows backoff and a terminal dead-letter after a bounded number of attempts.
18.04.03.negative: A retry never repeats non-idempotent side effects without a stable provider operation key.
18.04.03.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.04.context: A marketplace has interchangeable shipping providers for domestic and international routes.
18.04.04.failure: Leaking provider-specific response schemas into domain code makes outages difficult to isolate.
18.04.04.correction: Normalize provider success, retryable failures and permanent errors behind typed adapters.
18.04.04.positive: A test double returns the same domain result shape for two simulated providers.
18.04.04.negative: A malformed or unknown provider payload cannot be treated as a successful shipment.
18.04.04.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.05.context: An integration API key should access delivery events but not payments or customer exports.
18.04.05.failure: One unrestricted administrator token for every workflow increases impact of a credential leak.
18.04.05.correction: Design per-provider least-privilege scopes, rotation and environment separation.
18.04.05.positive: A key inventory maps each credential to a small capability and an owner.
18.04.05.negative: A webhook verifier key cannot also initiate payouts or export tenant data.
18.04.05.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.06.context: An external partner changes its webhook schema between two API versions.
18.04.06.failure: Assuming new provider fields are always present makes upgrades corrupt stored events.
18.04.06.correction: Version request and response contracts and maintain backward-compatible adapter fixtures.
18.04.06.positive: Both supported versions normalize to an explicit stable internal event.
18.04.06.negative: An unknown incompatible version fails closed and is retained for review.
18.04.06.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.07.context: A developer reproduces a provider outage without paying for live API traffic.
18.04.07.failure: Mocks that always succeed conceal timeouts, duplicate callbacks and schema drift.
18.04.07.correction: Use a deterministic fake with scripted 429, timeout, duplicate event and malformed response cases.
18.04.07.positive: The local test double drives a bounded retry and successful deduplication state transition.
18.04.07.negative: The fake is never presented as proof of actual provider availability or DNS configuration.
18.04.07.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.

18.04.08.context: A subscription service accepts a signed renewal webhook and records an inbox event.
18.04.08.failure: Trusting the event's JSON tenant field without signature validation enables account takeover or billing spoofing.
18.04.08.correction: Verify the raw signed payload, freshness and provider-specific delivery ID before any domain mutation.
18.04.08.positive: A signed event is accepted once and retry processing can recover a pending record.
18.04.08.negative: A forged signature, stale event or duplicated delivery never causes a second side effect.
18.04.08.caveat: The teaching inbox verifies an illustrative HMAC envelope, not an actual provider-specific signature convention; durable inbox storage and real provider tests remain required.
